appSubtitle: Learn how electric coils shape magnetic fields

injection.title: Particle Injection
injection.hint: Navigate with WASD + arrow keys. Arrow keys look around; WASD moves. Press Space to inject a particle.

descriptions.singleLoop: A single circular current loop produces a dipole-like magnetic field. The field lines form closed loops threading through the coil. On the axis, the field falls off as 1/(a²+z²)^(3/2).
descriptions.helmholtz: Two coaxial coils separated by their radius create a remarkably uniform field region between them — the Helmholtz configuration. Widely used in laboratory setups to cancel the Earth's field.
descriptions.antiHelmholtz: With the lower coil's current reversed the two coils repel each other's flux, creating an anti-Helmholtz (magnetic mirror) configuration. The field is zero at the midplane and strong at each coil — useful for trapping particles.
descriptions.toroidal: Arranging N coils symmetrically around a torus creates a toroidal magnetic field. Charged particles can be confined in such a geometry — the basis of tokamak and stellarator fusion reactors.
descriptions.tokamak: Adds a central plasma current Iₚ to the toroidal coil field. The current flows in the toroidal (φ) direction; by Ampère's law it induces a poloidal field that wraps around the minor cross-section. Together the toroidal and poloidal components create helical field lines — the hallmark of tokamak confinement. The rotational transform ι (field-line winding number) is set by the ratio of poloidal to toroidal field strength.
descriptions.gradient: A purely analytical field where Bz varies in the x-direction: Bz(x) = B₀ + α·x² + β·x⁴, with Bx = By = 0. The field is divergence-free since ∂Bz/∂z = 0. α > 0 concentrates field lines near x = 0 (stronger field in the center). α < 0 pushes field strength to the edges — a transverse gradient relevant to MRI and plasma confinement.
descriptions.helicalSheet: A radial line of starting points is advected along field lines. The rotational transform iota(r) ∝ r causes outer lines to wind faster, shearing the initial straight line into a helical sheet.
